items.text: Four rounds in, nobody in this group has laid a glove on SC Magdeburg: four wins from four, 141 goals scored against 108 conceded, and top spot with eight points. Kolstad Håndball sit at the other extreme without a single point, shipping 143 goals across the same four outings — close to 36 a night against tonight's visitors. That gulf in two-way quality is exactly what a short handicap is built for. The bet is SC Magdeburg -1.5 goals, and our outright winner call is SC Magdeburg.

items.text: Boston Bruins have turned TD Garden into an awkward place to visit early this season: 3-1-0 on home ice inside a 7-2-1 overall record, a .750 points percentage and 15 goals scored to just six conceded in front of their own crowd. Nashville Predators, by contrast, arrive at 3-2-3 and .563 with a negative goal difference, relying on overtime points to stay respectable. Rather than chase the short moneyline, take the cushion: our selection is Boston Bruins +0.5 on the puck line, which lands unless Boston Bruins lose in regulation, and we make Boston Bruins the match-winner call as well.

These two are travelling in opposite directions. Florida Panthers walk into PPG Paints Arena at 5-2-2, carrying a .667 points percentage, a three-game winning streak and a healthy 3-1-2 return from their road games so far. Pittsburgh Penguins have lost four straight, sit at 3-6-1 and .350, and own a minus-five goal difference despite playing at home tonight. Florida's form line is stronger in every column the NHL publishes, so the play is Florida Panthers +0.5 with the puck-line cushion — it only needs the Panthers to dodge a regulation defeat — with Florida Panthers also named as our winner pick.

The IRL's official world rankings, calculated over the current season and the three before it, put Tonga fifth on 54% of the maximum ranking points and Lebanon down in 23rd on just 7% — the widest gap between any two sides meeting in this World Cup round at CommBank Stadium. Rankings that far apart usually translate into field position Lebanon cannot defend for eighty minutes, even allowing for tournament nerves in Round 2. Our selection is Tonga -10.5 points on the handicap, and Tonga are the clear match-winner call.

items.text: Australia's Jillaroos hold the maximum 100% mark at the summit of the IRL women's rankings, while England Women, third in that same official list, carry only 40% — a sixty-point chasm between first and third that tells you how far ahead of the field the Jillaroos currently sit. England Women are no soft touch, yet on Australian soil at HBF Park in Perth the ranking evidence points one way. Back Australia Jillaroos -15.5 points; the straight winner call is also Australia Jillaroos.

items.text: Bayonne's home date with LOU Rugby brings together fifth against eighth in the official Top 14 table after six rounds, and the recent momentum sits with the hosts: Bayonne banked three consecutive wins over Clermont, Racing 92 and Paris before last week's defeat in Toulouse, whereas LOU Rugby's form strip shows three straight losses coming into this trip. With Jean Dauger behind them, Bayonne get our vote outright, and our selection is Aviron Bayonnais +1.5 points, a line that still pays out if they fall by a single point.

Australia top the IRL men's world rankings with the maximum 100% rating, and Sunday's opponents Fiji stand seventh on 34% in the same official list — fewer than half the ranking points of the Kangaroos across the four-year cycle the IRL measures. Add a Suncorp Stadium crowd in Brisbane behind the home side for this Round 2 meeting and the ranking gap should widen, not narrow, over eighty minutes. The selection is Australia -17.5 points on the handicap, with Australia the obvious winner call.
